title: Johnston Island scuttlebutt: Soviet orbital nuke shot down, object recovered

tellings.quote: First of all something had fallen down toward the island from that explosion in the sky. The explosion lit up the entire South Pacific and and caused all sorts of alarm and reports of UFOs and so on. And something had been recovered.
We were told that what happened is the the Soviets had launched a nuke into orbit up above us and JFK told Krushov, "Take that down."
tellings.difference: Adds that JFK told Khrushchev to take it down, and frames the UFO shootdown as a cover for the Soviet nuke.
tellings.link_reason: Same Johnston Island scuttlebutt that a Soviet orbital nuke was shot down, relayed by Bob Jacobs.

as_told.title: Johnston Island rumor: UFO shootdown covered a Soviet nuke

related.note: Same Johnston Island event, with something falling from the blast and being recovered. Here the object is explained as a Soviet orbital nuke that was shot down, not a UFO.

plain: Around 1962, the talk on Johnston Island, a tiny Pacific atoll, was that an explosion high in the sky lit up the whole South Pacific, set off UFO reports, and that something fell toward the island and was recovered. Bob Jacobs, who says he was told this, tells it to Michels, and Michels repeats it on another episode. In Jacobs's version the Soviets had put a nuclear weapon into orbit above them, JFK told Khrushchev "Take that down," and the UFO shootdown story covered for the Soviet nuke. If true, a recovered object and a hidden nuclear standoff lie behind the sightings.
